The game is really simple to pick up. You press only one button! Its in the title!!! But its anything but easy. The difficulty throughout the campaign has been very well balanced so far. It's never impossibly hard, but it also doesn't hold your hand. The rift mode also adds a ton of replayability. There is SO MUCH to try out with all the potential weapon and build combinations. I'm really impressed they managed to incorporate so many complex movement/attacking mechanics, while being restricted to only one button. If you're a fan of bullet hell or rhythm type games, or just want something a bit more accessible, then this game is a perfect fit.

Dialogue is funny and the story line is linear and smooth. I love it it and will definitely challenge my friends at this. Only downside it is very addictive.

非常推荐，全关卡通关以及评分榜内容全解锁。 难度不俗的弹幕射击游戏。中后期关卡难度略高，但并不是没有容错，评分榜到达特定分数可以获得增加一滴血上限的能力，四滴血玩下来我觉得在所有关卡里头都可以从容通过，实在太难的死多几次还是能背板过的。武器、移动方式以及被动能力方面，虽然各都设计了好几种选择，但其实能用的不多，我用的最多的是激光以及最初始的turn移动，被动自然还是选择+1HP上限，容错大大增加。部分音效跟just shapes &beats有点像，但可惜bgm却只有一首。 肉鸽模式类似爬塔的可玩性也很不错，一些新boss只会在肉鸽模式里出现。随着获得的能力越来越多，玩起来也是很爽的，但后期的敌人血条动不动五六条，boss七八条的，着实还是很难打的，目前暂未打通。 游戏体量虽然不大，但是只有一个按键的设计，并有如此高的完成度，还是值得一个好评的。

This looked like a really cool game when I first saw it. I love boss rush games like titan souls, and the 1 button twists on games like Rhythm Doctor or Rhythm Heaven made me think this would be similar. After beating the campaign in under 3 hours, while getting top times on most of the levels, I found that ONE BTN BOSSES is an unpolished, unplaytested, poorly designed game, that rides on an enticing premise. ---------- Good stuff: -The premise is great. There's a lot you can do with this one button, on-rail movement type of stuff. -The shooting mechanics based off of speed are great too. Creates that nice depth with a balance between dodging and DPS. -I found the dialogue funny at times, and the office premise surprised me. -The build mechanics are cool. You get a module for movement, damage, and a supporting one, and there's potential for cool synergies between all of these. There's also room for building around bosses, using certain movement and damage abilities that work well with the bosses attacks. Unfortunately, despite all the potential here, I rarely found moments where I had to swap my build to counter a boss, and there is one build that 200% outperforms any other build. -I like that the game focuses on time to defeat a boss, rather than just defeating the boss. This gives room for casual and hardcore players. -I couldn't find any bugs related to gameplay. I only found one minor UI bug that doesn't impact the game experience. That's really all the good stuff I could find. ---------- Bad stuff: -There is a huge lack of polish and content throughout the whole game. This will be expanded on in the rest of the review, but also this is the 1.0 release, and there is a feedback google form in the pause screen. I understand the desire for feedback, but just plug socials or a discord, or be in early access. A google form in your *pause* menu is embarrassing. -Despite being a boss rush game, there is only 5 unique bosses. Now, each of these bosses do have multiple encounters and if you consider all of that it's probably around 30-40 bosses. But most of the encounters on the same boss are the same attack styles over and over. Many of the attacks are uninteresting, and they will mix and match attacks together only to create walls and poorly telegraphed messes. Despite the on-rail restrictiveness of the movement, it's clear the devs did not think about how the player is supposed to dodge some of these attacks, and instead just put stuff they thought was kinda cool. Compare this to other boss rush games like Titan Souls or Rabbit And Steel, which have many more boss designs, with varied unique attack patterns, that are all well telegraphed, and there is thought put into what the player is supposed to do. If there was more thought put into these attack patterns, with a clear goal in mind of how each attack/phase in a boss is supposed to challenge the player, this could be really really fun. But instead it feels random, like not even unfair random, it just feels like spam. If they went with a more reactive approach with boss design, rather than set pattern attacks for each boss, that would service the movement mechanics much better. -There are these HR fights before each boss that teach you the attacks of the boss. This seems like a cool idea, it lessens any BS of "wtf is going on." But there are already infinite fast retries with no consequences, so you could just play the boss once or twice and get the gist of the attacks. And the learning phase of a boss is one of the most fun parts of bossfight games. The learning is part of why soulslike games, Hollow Knight, shmups, are so fun and exhilarating. You get to the hard part, freak out and go "wtf is going on" and die, and then you slowly learn the patterns and realize that everything is actually pretty simple. In ONE BTN BOSSES, you don't get any of that learning experience, and rather you just memorize un-telegraphed patterns and it's just tedious. -There is a lack of QOL throughout the game. There are some obvious changes that should be there but aren't: there's no "fully charged" indicator for the reverse module, there's no way to change your build in the pause screen, there's disappearing telegraph for the drop attacks but not for the similar bomb attacks, you can't see your time in game, you can't see the time to get certain ranks, you can't find damage numbers for your attacks, there's no additional damage stats in the roguelike pickups so you can't minmax your build, and more small things that add up and break your immersion. -I think the art style is cool, but the way it's executed is honestly ugly. Everything looks very jagged when there are off-angled shapes: many outlines, like the arc attacks in the first level, have this problem. The victory and defeat screens look blurry. The symbols in the grind rewards don't fully fill the outline, so there's some empty pixels that look weird. When choosing your supportive item on the build select, the lines in the middle don't reach the info box and just float there. Also, every fight has the exact same background. There is absolutely no styling or other distinctions for each stage, besides the boss sprite and attack patterns. -I saved the biggest one for the end, the worst part about this game are the modules and the builds. There are 3 movement options, 5 attack options, and 7 utility options. Here are the useless ones: -I could not find a use for reverse movement. It's clunky and doesn't synergize with any of the attacks. You deal much more damage and have much more mobility with turn or dash. -Pickup attack is overcomplicated and useless. It deals no damage and requires you to have perfect position to grab the pickup as much as possible, but there's always something in the way and the damage is weak. I think it's supposed to synergize with dash but for some stupid stupid reason you can't pickup the pickup while dashing??? -Juggler attack has the same problems as pickup but at least it scales. -Shooter attack is fine but laser is a direct upgrade. -Slower not weaker is a complete debuff and I don't even know why it exists, you don't even get a damage buff. -Phaser is situational and underwhelming. -Basically all utilities are weaker than thick hull and invincibl-er The laser attack is a million times better than 3/4 of the other attacks, and then that last attack is completely busted and untested. How the reload attack is supposed to work is you click, it charges up, and then it shoots once its fully charged, or you click again to shoot it prematurely. The fully charged attack does a lot of damage, but because of how poor the boss attacks are, you can't get a full charge. So how you're actually supposed to play reload is by mashing your mouse and space bar as fast as you can, melting the bosses with a ton of small bullets with a high minimum damage. They somehow did not test this and it completely ruins the whole game if you decide to play like this. It's 30 seconds faster than any other build and when combined with thick hull or invincibl-er, it's just a button mashing simulator. ---------- Basically, a combination of bad boss patterns and unbalanced untested builds creates a very brainless, poorly thought out experience. Even if you play without an overpowered build, the way the bullet hells are designed makes it a frustrating memory-fest. Most of the potential in this game is squandered due to the exact wrong decisions being made. Because of how great the base concepts are, a lot of this could be fixed in patches and this could be a really great game. That's the only reason I wrote this review, because this game could be super fun if they actually paid attention to how they designed the game. So please release many many patches, and then I'll recommend this game.

A great bullet hell boss rush game. Thoroughly enjoyed my time with it and couldn't stop playing it until I beat it. It took me less than 3 hours to do so (beating every level) and there's apparently a true ending where you have to do some grinding which I didn't do, but overall I'm satisfied with my experience. A more punchy soundtrack could have enhanced the experience, not to mention bosses reacting to the music. Other than that, there are a whole lot of upgrades to unlock to find your favorite playstyle but bear in mind that some bosses benefit from a specific combo of them which also felt like a nice change of pace. There's also a story here, but it's just made to give some sense of progression, you won't find anything deep or interesting here. Oh and it has a roguelike mode if you're into that, and it's well done from what I saw in a single playthrough. Great work to the devs, keep it up! 3.5/5

[h2][i]One BTN Boss[/i] is a unique bullet hell game that focuses on minimal input with maximum execution – ★★★⯪☆ [/h2] [h3][b]One-tap Wins:[/b][/h3] ✅ [b][i]Accessible gameplay that is all about precision.[/i][/b] Using only a single input, the game strips away complexity in controls which makes it easy to pick up and learn. The focus is mainly on timing, reaction, and precision, learning enemy patterns and knowing which weapons, abilities, and supports to use for each level. ✅ [b][i]Complementary roguelike gameplay.[/i][/b] There is another mode where you can engage in a roguelike gameplay through rifts and build up abilities and skills to pass wave 5. It's a very simple roguelike setup, but provides more variety to the gameplay beyond the standard levels. ✅ [b][i]High replayability.[/i][/b] There is a tight feedback loop to game: you die, restart instantly, and get back to the fight. Mistakes can be overlooked with the quick restart key, and this makes it easier and more enjoyable to S rank a level. ✅ [b][i]Stylish Presentation.[/i][/b] The visuals are minimalist but sharp, using simple graphics to provide focus on the bullets to avoid and where your cursor is. [h3][b]Tap Outs:[/b][/h3] ⚠️ [b][i]May be a steep learning curve for some.[/i][/b] While the controls are simple, the actual gameplay isn't easy, and it might take time to get used to how the game works. The bosses also hit hard, the timing windows can be tight, and there’s little room for error. ⚠️ [b][i]It's not a rhythm game.[/i][/b] Despite the rhythm tag, the game's soundtrack has no influence on how you play. It's better described as a bullet hell boss rush with a roguelike mode on the side. ⚠️ [b][i]Crashes more often than I'd prefer.[/i][/b] The game tends to crash after playing for a while, particularly when I have quick restarted a level multiple times. It's not too much of an issue when concerning overall progression (because of the constant auto-saves), but it could be a problem if it crashes during a level, though I haven't experienced it before.

The attacks and moves are not balanced as in choosing the "right" ones can be the difference between S rank and D rank. The progression is a bit unrewarding with a lot of colour palettes that just strain your eyes while playing.

tl;dr this game is only worth it on a deep discount as it's just eh. It's kinda underwhelming and i cba to format properly so here are my main gripes - the upgrades don't feel good at all and i found myself always going back to the basic loadout because it was viable and worked well on every level. why would i even use the new "cool" thing if i just feel like it performs worse in every way. call it a skill issue or whatever i call it bad design. - the roguelike mode kinda exacerbates this issue and it's quite uhhh... boring, especially with the "secret" exodia upgrade. - IF you take some of the other movement options then just be prepared to get undodgeable combos. again, the base swap is king. - even if you want to 100% the game for fun, the achievements are more annoying and you'll just find yourself googling the ideal build for each stage. have fun! - the colour schemes are god awful and whoever came up with some of them must be blind. i'm so glad i got the automatically applied "reward" that ruins the game. - rhythm? no i don't care to list the positives.

The game teaches you that "red is bad" and then plops dozens of other harmless, frantically moving red objects on the screen at a time.

Whoever thought it made sense to include identity politics and sexual preference references in what is otherwise a cute little auto-shooter game featuring no actual people or story line must be some kind of nonce. Really bizarre and offputting.

Highly likely this game is just not for me. It starts of as a boss rush game where you can grind and can hunt for a high-score. The game gives you GP(Grind Points) to unlock gear, which in theory should help you beat the bosses. Personally I don´t think these upgrades actually help with anything. Some weapons feel utterly unplayable and some movement things are funny but I do not see how they are supposed to help you. It is definitely not expected that you beat the bosses on your first try. A lot of moves are just spawn funny shape inside you or undodgeable at your current position. Which would be fine if the grinding is rewarding or at least fun. Due to the simple gameplay playing the game can feel like a drag if you want to get back to the phase you died at and for me actually beating the boss felt kinda empty. So actually grinding for the win just was a throw head against the wall situation without the fun part of other games. I guess the colors are neat but most of them where confusing in a already visually exhausting game. On the plus sides: Music was great, the writing was funny at times and it looks good when you are allowed to see the game. Is it a bad game probably not, but its just not a game a had a lot of fun with.

One BTN Bosses is a deceptively simple game that packs a punch with its one-button mechanic, the depth of the roguelike customization, and adrenaline-pumping gameplay. It’s perfect for players seeking a challenging but rewarding bullet-hell experience. It took roughly 3+ hours to complete the main campaign, and I plan on jumping back into the roguelike gameplay to see how far I can go before losing my mind. It’s a great game with tons of replay ability, with the ranked level completion and the roguelike section of the game. If you are looking for a challenge with fun, colorful graphics and intense gameplay, it’s a must-play. I highly recommend it—Inner Sloth is now two-for-two for me with the games they publish: One BTN Bosses and Clickolding. I am excited to check out more of the games they have coming soon.

C+ 有趣的概念+极其糟糕的执行=没什么巧克力味的屎 进度：打完第四个boss放弃，负反馈过强，正反馈只靠自己的通关念想独木难支 优点： 1. 极好的概念出发点。看到本作的概念时真的眼前一亮，用一个按键改变方向（后续解锁其他能力），固定轨道躲避各式各样的弹幕，不转向伤害越来越高，high risk high reward 2. 干净的游戏美术。弹幕呈现清晰，图像看着很干脆利落，有一个很贴切的单词crisp 3. 不仅只有一种躲避方式，还有冲刺、折返蓄力等，可扩展性还不错（虽然我觉得这些都不如最普通的转向用的舒服） 缺点： 1. 概念很好，但是执行是一坨屎。 a. 转向带来的巨量负反馈，只因为躲避弹幕就需要受到惩罚。既然游戏中会有弹幕不停攻击轨道，那么玩家只要不断转向，敌人就很难攻击到玩家（但中后期其实就算不断转向也很容易对不到轴受伤），那么策划给出的答案是，玩家初始攻击力很残缺，只有通过不转向积累速度才能较快地解决boss，要不然就会刮痧。乍一看好像没啥问题，实际上，转向=DPS低=BOSS打的慢=更长的战斗时间=更多的压力=更少的结算分数=越来越多的负反馈，这个游戏每一次转向都附带了非常多连锁的负反馈，且，躲避有且只带来躲避弹幕成功这个可能性的反馈，很多时候如果连弹幕都没有躲避成功就会是成吨的负反馈。设计思路不应该是：躲避弹幕无明显惩罚，长时间不躲避弹幕给予高奖励，现状是：躲避弹幕有明显惩罚，且躲错了有极高惩罚，长时间不躲避弹幕奖励也没高到哪里去，因为目押弹幕就需要高频率地转向。策划并没有提供一个持续躲避合理的DPS，而是给到了一个相当刮痧的数值，导致专注躲避的体验非常糟糕。尤其是中高难度boss弹幕密度极高，甚至有部分弹幕招式强迫玩家在极小范围内不断转向，玩家宛如无能的丈夫，只能躲避完全不能输出 b. 从弹幕游戏到对轴游戏的难绷转变。而我打了半小时就产生了疑问：既然弹幕那么多，那为什么分数要求经常给我感觉很高呢？大部分关卡我明明尽可能地不躲避了，还只有C的分数，结果在一次我稍微走神忘记操作的时候，我发现我停下来的几秒钟，没有收到任何伤害，这一关的开局我什么都不用动，就可以安安心心输出，弹幕完全是摆设？！带着这个猜想，我开始在一些高压关卡故意不动，我发现相当多（甚至我觉得可能是全部）关卡boss的攻击都有一些特定timing的轴（时间点），在这个轴转向就可以站桩几秒钟，躲掉所有的弹幕，放弃一切交互，于是本游戏就从我看到弹幕，思考弹幕躲避时机的弹幕游戏，变成了我开局找到一个类似于安定点的轴的对轴游戏，那么设计出来那么多的弹幕有什么意义？？？ 2. 极多弹幕非常不符合直觉，且不具备完备的提示系统，导致弹幕躲避体验部分时间极其抓瞎。从中期开始，一些弹幕的timing就非常难以琢磨，快慢刀神经刀双管齐下，有些固定攻击玩家位置的，从千里之外就开始描线，却完全没有显示速度、距离，玩家根本不能通过这条线推理出大概什么时候这个弹幕会到达轨道的哪个部分从而早期预警；一些占轨道位置的并不会有倒计时提示什么时候会消失，导致为了稳妥起见玩家会提前转向，这个时候弹幕又很难绷地消失了 3. 大部分升级并没有什么使用欲望，如冲刺、蓄力转向、回旋镖，感觉都远不如默认的好用，升级系统形同虚设（虽然颜色模板都还挺好看的） 4. 肉鸽模式味如嚼蜡，目前遇到的都是数值提升，全程三滴血，就不像是让人卡关的时候放松心情的...
